questions.stem: Why does pentane (C5H12) have a higher boiling point than methane (CH4)?

options.text: Pentane has stronger covalent bonds within its molecules
Pentane has stronger intermolecular forces because it is a larger molecule
Pentane has ionic bonds as well as covalent bonds
Methane is a gas so it has already boiled

questions.explanation: Pentane is a larger molecule than methane, with more electrons and a greater surface area. This means the intermolecular forces (van der Waals forces) between pentane molecules are stronger, so more energy is needed to overcome them, resulting in a higher boiling point.
